text: Problem set 10 Problem 1. (i) Show that A ∈ Mn×n(F ) is invertible if and only if it has no 0 eigenvalue. (ii) Let A be invertible and v be an eigenvector of A with eigenvalue λ. Show that v is an eigenvector of A−1 with eigenvalue λ−1. Moreover, show that pA−1(x) = (−1)n det(A) xnpA( 1 x ). (iii) Let A ∈ Mn×n(F ) be invertible. Show that A is diagonalizable over F if and only if A−1 is diagonalizable over F . Hint: For (ii) use the identity xI − A−1 = −xA−1( 1 x I − A). Problem 2. Let A, B ∈ Mn×n(C). We define the commutator as [A, B] = AB − BA. Show that there is no A, B ∈ Mn×n(C) such that [A, B] = I. Hint: What is tr([A, B])? Remark 1. Note that if P and Q are as in Example 3.27, then [P, Q] = I. The difference is that P, Q are linear transformations on infinite dimensional vector space. That [P, Q] = I is one of the axioms of quantum mechanics. Since such operators do not exist on finite dimensional vector spaces, quantum mechanics studies operators on infinite dimensional spaces e.g. the space of square integrable functions L2(R3). (ii) Show that if A ∈ Mn×n(F ) is diagonalizable over F , then f (A) is also diagonal- izable over F . (iii) Let A = (5 −3 6 −4 ) Consider f (x) = x2025 + x ∈ R[x]. Compute f (A), tr(f (A)), and det(f (A)). You can use the results from Homework 9 Problem 1. You do not need to evaluate large powers. Problem 4. Let λ1, . . . , λm ∈ R be distinct real numbers. Let V be the subpsace of C(R) given by span(eλ1x, . . . , eλmx). Let D : V → C(R) be the linear transformation given by D(f ) = f ′ where f ′ means the derivative of f . (i) Show that im D ⊂ V . (ii) Show that D(eλix) = λieλix for i = 1, . . . , m. (iii) Show that eλ1x, . . . , eλmx are linearly independent. 1 Optional exercises related to Lecture 10 Do NOT submit this with your homework.
